title: Finite-free internal Hom preserves exact sequences in arbitrary universes
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $P$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with a specified isomorphism $P\cong\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$ for a natural number $r$. Let $S=(S_1\xrightarrow{f}S_2\xrightarrow{g}S_3)$ be a short complex with $gf=0$ that is exact at $S_2$; no injectivity of $f$ or surjectivity of $g$ is required. Then postcomposition defines a short complex $\mathcal Hom(P,S_1)\to\mathcal Hom(P,S_2)\to\mathcal Hom(P,S_3)$ exact at its middle term. The site object universe, site morphism universe, and module-section universe may be different; internal Hom has the maximum of these universes.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 via Tag 0GM7, case (2); explicit finite-free Hom calculation

proof.text: Obtain left exact abelian sheafification in section universes w and max(u,v,w) from the existing weak sheafification and locally-bijective characterization. This supplies the abelian module-sheaf categories and the exact forgetful functors used below.

Prove restriction to Over U preserves finite limits by sectionwise evaluation. For every fixed source P, the evaluated internal Hom functor, followed by forgetting the module structure, is naturally the composite of sheaf-to-presheaf restriction and coyoneda from P restricted to Over U. These functors preserve finite limits. Reflect the limit through the module forgetful functor, sectionwise evaluations, and the fully faithful inclusion of sheaves. Thus internal Hom from P preserves finite limits, without any freeness assumption.

For an epi f:M→N, the exact forgetful functor to abelian sheaves shows that f is locally surjective. Given a section φ of Hom(P,N) over U, evaluate φ on the finite basis b_i=ιFree_i≫e.inv. Intersect the finitely many image sieves, a covering also for the empty index set. On every arrow k:V→U in this covering, choose lifts m_i of the basis images. Form the actual restricted morphism ψ=Σ_i G(p_i.val)≫unitLift(m_i), where G is restriction to Over V and p_i=e.hom≫freeπ_i. Naturality and linearity show unitLift(m_i)≫G(f.val)=G(b_i.val)≫φ|V. The identity Σ_i p_i≫b_i=id_P, obtained from the existing sum_freeπ_ιFree lemma, proves ψ≫f=φ|V. Consequently Hom(P,f) is locally surjective and hence epi.

Apply Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels to F=homFunctor(R).obj(op P). Exact.map transports hS to S.map F, and the functorial zero equation of S.map F supplies the existential witness. Its maps are definitionally the two homObjMap maps in the statement.
